children: Alumis announced LUMUS Phase 2b topline results: the trial missed primary and secondary endpoints overall but showed robust responses in IFNGS‑high patients.
LUMUS did not meet primary (BICLA at Week 48) or key secondary endpoints in the overall SLE population, reducing overall efficacy.
Prespecified IFNGS‑high subgroup showed robust responses on BICLA, SRI‑4, CLASI‑50 and LLDAS, supporting Phase 3 development.
Higher-than-expected IFNGS‑low enrollment (~40%) raised placebo response and diluted overall trial results.
Pharmacodynamics showed dose‑dependent interferon‑pathway target engagement, maximal at 40 mg BID, and no new safety signals observed.
Alumis remains on track to submit an NDA for envudeucitinib in moderate‑to‑severe plaque psoriasis in 4Q 2026 and will seek End of Phase 2 meetings on SLE Phase 3 design.

title: Alumis reports Phase 2b LUMUS: missed overall endpoints but strong IFNGS‑high subgroup; NDA for psoriasis on track
